recorded.prompt:q-reversed: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-reversed: The reversed row allows `10` and refuses `01`: it says "if $`b`$ then $`a`$", a different rule that the solver will enforce without complaint.
recorded.prompt:q-joint-premise: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-joint-premise: "If $`a`$ and $`b`$, then $`c`$." $`x_a + x_b - 1`$ is 1 when both are funded and 0 or $`-1`$ otherwise, so the row $`x_a + x_b - 1 \le x_c`$ forces $`x_c = 1`$ only when both are funded.
recorded.prompt:q-credit-side: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-credit-side: In the reward, the solver wants $`y`$ large ... So the "down" rows matter: they keep $`y_r = 0`$ where there is no work. With the "up" rows alone, the solver sets all four to 1 and claims $25,936k while the plan serves only 3 regions

recorded.prompt:q-reversed:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-reversed:b: "The reversed row allows `10` and refuses `01`". 10 is A without B (allowed), and 01 is B without A (refused). That is the opposite of option b.
recorded.prompt:q-reversed:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-reversed:c: The table row "a -> b, reversed   x_a >= x_b   00 10 11" allows 10 (A alone).
recorded.prompt:q-reversed:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-reversed:d: "a different rule that the solver will enforce without complaint."
recorded.prompt:q-joint-premise:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-joint-premise:a: By the page's check ("A row says what you mean if it allows exactly the 0/1 combinations the logic allows"): with R alone, 1 <= x_T forces T, and with both funded, 2 <= x_T allows no plan. The row refuses combinations the rule allows.
recorded.prompt:q-joint-premise:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-joint-premise:c: "'If $`a`$ or $`b`$, then $`c`$' can also be written as the single row $`x_a + x_b \le 2\,x_c`$." That is the OR premise, so R alone would force T.
recorded.prompt:q-joint-premise:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-joint-premise:d: "'If $`a`$ or $`b`$, then $`c`$.' This is two implications ... so two rows: $`x_a \le x_c`$ and $`x_b \le x_c`$." That is the OR rule, not the AND rule.
recorded.prompt:q-credit-side:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-credit-side:a: "With the 'up' rows alone, the solver sets all four to 1 and claims $25,936k while the plan serves only 3 regions"
recorded.prompt:q-credit-side:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-credit-side:b: The up rows y_c >= x_i "force $`y_r = 1`$ wherever there is work", and a reward makes the solver want y large anyway.
recorded.prompt:q-credit-side:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-credit-side:d: "the solver sets all four to 1". A plan exists, and y = 1 satisfies every up row.
